kept.title: Swing You Sinners! (frame)
kept.caption: Bimbo and a rooster in a 1930 Fleischer frame, both with smooth tube limbs and white-gloved noodle hands and no elbows or knees.
kept.credit: Public domain (Fleischer Studios), via Wikimedia Commons

kept.title: Betty Boop and Bimbo
kept.caption: Bimbo's black bean body with plain dot-and-lid eyes stands beside Betty's huge lashed eyes, so the two eye conventions sit in one image.

kept.title: Betty in Blunderland (frame)
kept.caption: Close-up of Betty Boop with an oversized round head, spit curls, heavy-lashed eyes, tiny nose and small mouth.
kept.credit: Public domain (Fleischer Studios), via Wikimedia Commons

kept.title: No! No! A Thousand Times No!! (frame)
kept.caption: Two characters swaying together on a bench in a 1935 short, a pose pair typical of whole bodies bobbing to the music beat (judge it with the next frame of the same scene).
kept.credit: Public domain (Fleischer Studios), via Wikimedia Commons

kept.title: Koko's Earth Control (frame)
kept.caption: A grinning sun and a crescent moon with human faces, a plain case of the anything-can-come-alive logic of Fleischer shorts.
kept.credit: Public domain (Fleischer Studios), via Wikimedia Commons

kept.title: Olive Oyl on a boat (Popeye Meets Sindbad)
kept.caption: Olive Oyl's limbs bend like green rubber tubes as she drapes over a stool on a 3D model boat.
